slot.brief: Sum of a series whose nth term is of the form 1/(n(n+k)); telescope to get a closed form in n.

stem: The sum $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{r(r+2)}$, for a positive integer $n$, is
working:
$\dfrac{1}{r(r+2)}=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac1r-\dfrac1{r+2}\right)$.\n$S_n=\dfrac12\left(1+\dfrac12-\dfrac1{n+1}-\dfrac1{n+2}\right)$.\n$S_n=\dfrac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}$.

Independent check: Use \(\frac1{r(r+2)}=\frac12(\frac1r-\frac1{r+2})\). The sum telescopes to \(\frac34-\frac1{2(n+1)}-\frac1{2(n+2)}=\frac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}\).
solution:
Using partial fractions,
$$\frac{1}{r(r+2)}=\frac12\left(\frac1r-\frac1{r+2}\right).$$
The sum telescopes: $S_n=\frac12\left(1+\frac12-\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}\right)=\boxed{\frac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}}$.
